calls.reason: Nye et al. found only 29% accuracy for unaided GPT-3 on narrative-state questions and recurring story inconsistencies. Gopher's knowledge results support the accompanying factual-recall strength.
The GPT-3 paper describes text prediction, while RAVEN finds both novelty and copying. Neither settles Marcus's philosophical judgment about scientific explanation or mere imitation.

The Gopher study reports scaling gains alongside substantial deficits on Winogrande, HellaSwag and PIQA. PaLM's reported gains do not contradict the limited claim that weaknesses remained on some measures.

Natural Instructions found uneven GPT-3 performance but also improved generalization to new tasks. The T5 study concerns a different setup; neither establishes the broader claim about absent abstraction and dependence on training particulars.

TruthfulQA found substantial falsehoods, Nye et al. found inconsistencies across all 50 generated stories, and the InstructGPT paper reported recurring fabrication despite improvements. Together they support the main reliability claim.

Razeghi et al. show term-frequency effects, not a matched seen-versus-unseen equation comparison. GPT-3's earlier arithmetic results suggest generalization, but limited exposure checks leave the learning mechanism unsettled.
